metadata.title: Claude, Client Intake.
metadata.purpose: Answer what a legal client-intake process has to get right first: not writing down the story, but catching a conflict of interest before hearing too much of it. Lands the carry-out that the conflict check comes before the details, not after.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carried unfilled '>' template placeholders at every skill-specific fact, and its named source_skill file does not exist on this machine -- see QUESTION.md. This redo reconstructs a generic, defensible client-intake account from the title/family rather than lifting facts that were never written.

beats.narration_text: Someone new to a legal practice figures client intake is paperwork -- write down what the prospective client says. It's not. It's gatekeeping -- catching a conflict before you say too much. Liam, take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Client intake -- is that just paperwork?', hesitates on 'paperwork', corrects to 'gatekeeping', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption is that intake means getting the story down carefully -- what happened, in the client's own words. But a flawless summary of that story is worthless if the firm already represents the other side in this exact dispute. Those notes get sealed, and the meeting should never have gone that far. What intake has to nail first is one question: who is on the other side.

shot.new_visual_element: A 'notes' card filling with careful handwriting; the whole card sealed shut the moment a matching name appears beneath it

production_viz.label: A flawless summary, sealed
production_viz.mechanic: A card labelled 'INTAKE NOTES' fills line by line with careful handwritten-style text. Beneath it, a small name field appears and lights up as a MATCH. The whole notes card immediately gets a heavy 'SEALED' stamp across it -- all that careful writing now unusable. A caption fades in: 'the meeting should never have gone that far.'

beats.narration_text: So the intake conversation runs in a fixed order, and the conflict check comes before anything else -- before the facts, before any advice. Watch the anchor: a prospective client calls about a dispute with their landlord and launches straight into the story. The very next question anyway is the landlord's name -- not "tell me more" -- checked against the firm's current clients before another word about the case.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- an intake order card (conflict check first, story second); a caller mid-story, paused on one blank field: landlord's name

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one question, asked first
production_viz.mechanic: A vertical order card: step 1 'CONFLICT CHECK' lit and large, step 2 'THE STORY' dim beneath it. THE ANCHOR. A speech-bubble trail representing the caller's story scrolls in from the left, mid-sentence, then freezes. A single blank field appears, labelled 'landlord's name', outlined only, waiting. THIS BLANK FIELD RETURNS, FILLED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The name comes back a match -- the firm already represents that landlord in an unrelated matter. Conflict flagged immediately, before a single privileged detail was on record. But a name that doesn't match anyone yet isn't a clean bill -- the other side might be a subsidiary of an existing client under a different name, so the check reruns whenever a new name surfaces. And clearing conflicts doesn't mean taking the case -- capacity, expertise, and fee still have to be decided.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the blank field lights up 'MATCH FOUND'; then split into a 'no match yet is not clear' card and a 'clear is not take the case' card

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- match found, and its limits
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 BLANK FIELD RETURNS, identical placement, and fills in with 'landlord's name' then flashes 'MATCH FOUND' in the accent colour, before the story trail resumes. It splits into two cards: left reads 'no match yet' with 'CLEAR' dimmed beneath it, labelled 'not proof there's no conflict'; right reads 'conflict clear' with 'TAKE THE CASE?' dimmed beneath it, labelled 'still needs capacity, expertise, fee'.

beats.narration_text: Client intake isn't writing down the story -- it's catching the conflict before you've heard too much of it. A gatekeeping question that comes after the details arrived too late.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. "I'm about to take an intake call with a new client. Before I let them tell me the whole story, help me write a short list of questions I need answered first -- starting with who's on the other side -- so I catch a conflict before I've heard anything I can't unhear." Liam, in for Bear.
